documents.title: Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of AGM
INTIMATION FOR RESCHEDULING OF 60TH ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE COMPANY ON 26TH AUGUST 2026 (WEDNESDAY) AT 12:00 NOON (IST)

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported its financial and operational results for Q4 and the full year FY2025-26, achieving a highest-ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT and record production volumes across several niche products. The management highlighted robust operational efficiencies, noting that gross refining margins (GRMs) for the full year stood at $9.2 per barrel while Q4 GRM reached $13.75 per barrel. The company also announced a final dividend recommendation of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend to INR62 per share for the year, alongside progress on capital expenditure projects such as Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS and retail outlets. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd reported a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT for FY2024-25, operating at 99.5% of its installed capacity. The full-year Gross Refining Margin (GRM) stood at $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year, primarily impacted by lower international product cracks.

demand_outlook.claim: The southern market for motor spirit shows a shortfall where production is less than demand by close to 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

demand_outlook.claim: Southern market growth for motor spirit is projected around 4%-5% while high-speed diesel growth forecast is at 3%.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has approved the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project with execution started in full swing.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: The retail outlet endeavor has started with 300 licenses taken and commissioning expected during the year.
capex_expansion.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

capex_expansion.claim: The total estimated cost for the LOBS project is INR1,600 crores and INR400 crores for the retail outlet project.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: The normal annual capex of the company is around INR500 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

capex_expansion.claim: Total capital expenditure spent during the current financial year was Rs. 673 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the Cauvery Basin Refinery project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CBR update, in the last year we revised the capital cost as well as the capital structure. The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

margins_costs.claim: The gross refining margin for quarter 4 was $13.75 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: Foreign exchange loss for the quarter was approximately INR200 crores and around INR350 crores for the full year.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: The full year GRM for 2024-25 was $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory gain for the quarter was $0.66 per barrel amounting to Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: The fuel and loss for the year came down to 8.51%.
margins_costs.quote: I must place it that if you remember our Energy Indexes and our Fuel and Loss Indexes were quite high 2-3 years back and we went to a roadmap where we said on a sustained basis, we will bring it down to very efficient levels and in that context, the fuel and loss has come down to 8.51% for the year as a whole.

margins_costs.claim: The total Gross Refining Margin was reported as 7995 Crore in 2022-23, 6146 Crore in 2023-24, and 1572 Crore in 9M 2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, which is equivalent to 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: In quarter 4, the company achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The new LOBS project will add a fresh capacity of 250,000 KTPA in Group 2 and Group 3.
orders_capacity.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

orders_capacity.claim: Crude throughput reached 10.45 MMT, which is equivalent to 99.5% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year

orders_capacity.claim: Quarter 4 crude throughput was 2.974 MMT, representing 113% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: and coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

capital_allocation.claim: The company's debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.18 on a gross level compared to 0.39 last year.
capital_allocation.quote: Our leverage position now stands at 0.18. Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: Gross borrowings stand at INR1,900 crores, while net borrowings are INR973 crores with a net debt ratio of 0.09.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores. If we consider net borrowing, the debt ratio is only 0.09, which is less than 0.1.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: The debt-to-equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: Total absolute debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores and net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024. Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share, representing 50% of the face value.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management noted that uncertainties due to logistical constraints and volatility of crude oil prices pose challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to the volatility of crude prices pose a challenge to operations.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

management_commitments.claim: Management expects the INR2,000 crores capex for the LOBS and retail outlet projects to be deployed over 2 to 3 years.
management_commitments.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: The company expects the ongoing debottlenecking study to be completed in the financial year 2026-27.
management_commitments.quote: But in the coming year, '26-'27, we hope that ongoing study will get completed.

management_commitments.claim: Maintenance CAPEX is expected to remain in the Rs. 200-250 crore range for the next year.
management_commitments.quote: Our maintenance CAPEX remains Rs. 200-250 crore range, and the next year forecast also, we feel the CAPEX will be in that range.

management_commitments.claim: Normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

management_commitments.claim: With the LOBS project, an additional Rs. 400 to Rs. 500 crores per year can be added to CAPEX for each of the next two years.
management_commitments.quote: And with this project, another Rs. 400 to Rs. 500 crores you can add for each of the year. So, without this project, about Rs. 300 crores per year. With this project, about Rs. 700 to Rs. 800 crores per year.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
